verdict.rationale: The evidence shows team-level credentials: the team's own provider key, a team key injected into CLIs, and per-member limits on which tools may be used. Nothing documents separate connected accounts or scoped tokens per end user of a customer's product, so each user's agent acting only on that user's own credentials is not shown. OAuth for 'your own account' and per-member tool permissions are related controls, not per-end-user credential isolation.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can maintain separate connected accounts and scoped tokens per end user of my product, so each user's agent acts only on that user's credentials
